A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 31-page versions of the same survey. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. The appendix pages are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 surveys existing research. Its method comparisons, dataset catalog, performance statements, and appendix prompt examples concern cited studies; it reports no original empirical results.

after.justification: v2 retains the same survey material. Its added Figure 2 is a conceptual workflow diagram, with no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or empirical data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the procedures described in Sections 3–7 are unchanged. Figure 2 illustrates the existing prompt-generation, evaluation, filtering, and iteration process without introducing a method component.

E1.justification: Section 13.2 and Tables 5–7 retain the same dataset and task catalog for surveyed methods. No training or evaluation scenario is added or revised.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain the same surveyed methods and classifications. Neither version reports an original experiment comparing the survey's framework against baselines.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics in Section 4 and model/settings information in Tables 2–4 are unchanged. No experiment or evaluation protocol is introduced or revised.

E4.justification: No ablation, sensitivity analysis, robustness test, or empirical case study is added or removed. Section 14 retains the same cited prompt examples.

E5.justification: No repeated-run information, random seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance-reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported findings and numerical examples are unchanged, including Section 4.3's cited win-rate increases of up to 22% for ChatGPT and 10% for GPT-4. Figure 2 contains no measured results.

T1.justification: Equation 1, both algorithms, Section 8's theoretical discussion, appendix notation, and tabulated complexity expressions are unchanged. The added flowchart introduces no mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: an APO formulation, a five-part unifying framework, literature categorization, and identification of future research directions.

C2.justification: Sections 9 and 11 retain the same discussion of task dependence, unclear mechanisms, scalability, multimodal research gaps, and survey limitations. The new diagram adds no substantive interpretation or qualification.

D1.justification: The appendix algorithms, model specifications, and prompt templates are unchanged. No implementation settings, reproducibility instructions, or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: The citations, reference list, excluded-work discussion in Section 12.2, and research positioning are unchanged. Reference pagination changes solely through text reflow.

P1.justification: Narrative prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization are unchanged. Apart from the added figure caption and routine version/date stamp, apparent text differences resolve to pagination and floating-table placement.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 2, 'Representative APO system,' on page 3. It illustrates seed initialization, candidate generation, evaluation, filtering, and the stopping/iteration loop. Its insertion reflows subsequent text; existing figures and tables are retained, and appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 provides a compact visual explanation of the existing APO workflow and iteration loop, complementing v1's taxonomy and pseudocode. This offers a modest improvement in explanatory accessibility; scientific content, literature coverage, and supporting appendices remain unchanged.
